title: Member Data pointer runs before replacement tab readiness after extension reload
surface: Hosted native member Data reload acceptance driver
organization_context: Approved member identity and organization were verified before reload; the exact saved row was cleaned up.
reproduction: Run 39461020039 on source ebe922a655b0bff320d1457e6b598bae3a1c1b10: after a successful replacement-worker open response and a distinct panel target/context, the first Data pointer sample has zero matching and visible tabs.

node --test tests/browser/data-member-reload-readiness.test.mjs failed against the old driver at pointer_target_not_unique for a controlled delayed-mount replacement; it passes with the readiness repair.
expected: Wait within the existing bounded panel-readiness interval until the adopted replacement target and frame match the owned panel and exactly one Data tab is visible, then send the trusted pointer and continue actual persistence assertions.
actual: The member driver called click(panel, 'title', 'Data') immediately after panel adoption. One matching SIDE_PANEL runtime context at 21 ms did not establish that React had mounted the Data tab; the pointer refused with zero targets before any post-reload Data assertion.
severity: S2: acceptance harness can stop at reload before measuring saved-pattern persistence; no persistent product bootstrap defect established.
cause: The Data reload path omitted the visible replacement-tab precondition that the shared Settings path already applies. The harness proved URL/context and replacement target, but dispatched the first Data pointer before checking mounted controls.
sibling_census: Settings replacement tab already used bounded readiness and remains on the shared helper. Scrape has a separate replacement-tab helper; this repair touches the member Data pointer path without changing its other lifecycle assertions or auth.
fix: Generalize the existing Settings tab readiness to a title-based shared helper, retaining the original interval. Member Data checks its adopted target ID, page/frame URL and one visible Data tab before the pointer; first/last bounded observations and failure stage are recorded without raw page contents. Never-ready, duplicate, wrong-target and wrong-frame results fail without input.
